# Issue tracker

Issues are tracked in **Linear** through the `linear` MCP server (configured in `opencode.json`; authenticate with `/mcps`).

## Workflow

Use the Linear MCP tools for issue operations in this repo. Do not use GitHub Issues or local `.scratch/` markdown issues unless the repo configuration changes.

Issue identifiers follow the format `ALE-123`.

Create issues with the appropriate team/project, title, description, and triage label/status.

## Tool usage

Tools come from the `linear` MCP server. Under Code Mode they are grouped as `tools.linear.*`; exact tool names evolve, so check the current catalog (e.g. `search({ query: "linear" })` in Code Mode) instead of guessing:

- Search/list, read, create, and update issues (the server has a unified save tool for create+update).
- Comments, labels, and workflow states.
- Projects, project milestones, and initiatives.

A read-only endpoint (`https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly`) exists, but this repo configures the read-write endpoint.

## Updating triage state

Apply the matching triage label/status string from `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` with the issue tools.

Repository: `alessandrojcm/dhc-dashboard`

## Workspace limits and housekeeping

- The team is `Alessandrojcm` (issue keys `ALE-123`). Its type labels are `Bug`, `Improvement`, and `Feature`, plus the team-level `wayfinder:*` labels and the triage labels `ready-for-agent` and `ready-for-human` (`list_issue_labels` without a team filter shows only the workspace labels, so pass `team: "Alessandrojcm"` and don't recreate them). The other triage strings in `triage-labels.md` (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `wontfix`) have no label: map them to the workflow state and state the triage role in the description. A ready issue gets its label plus the `Todo` state.
- A spec assembled from a wayfinder map is a new issue, not a child of the map: map children carry exactly one `wayfinder:*` label. Mention the map and its child tickets in the description (Linear links mentioned identifiers as related automatically) and comment on the map with the spec link.
- Implementation tickets broken out of a spec are sub-issues of the spec issue (`parentId`), labelled `Feature` + `ready-for-agent` in `Todo`, created blockers-first so `blockedBy` can name real identifiers.
- `save_issue` returns the new identifier in `id` (there is no `identifier` field). On create it can silently drop one entry of a multi-item `blockedBy`, so read every ticket back with `get_issue({ includeRelations: true })`, compare against the intended edges, and re-add any missing blocker with `save_issue({ id, blockedBy })`.
- The workspace is on Linear's free plan. Creating an issue fails with `You've exceeded the free issue limit for this workspace` once the active-issue cap is reached; archiving issues frees capacity.
- To archive in bulk, use `linctl graphql` (linctl has no archive subcommand): list `issues(filter:{state:{name:{eq:"Done"}}})`, then run `mutation($id:String!){ issueArchive(id:$id){ success } }` per id. When calling `linctl graphql --query` in a shell loop, redirect stdin from `/dev/null`; otherwise linctl treats the loop's stdin as a second query source and rejects every call.

## Projects & milestones

- Feature tickets may target the `DHC Dashboard` project for release grouping.
- Project milestones are supported by the Linear MCP tools (create/edit project milestones, add/remove issues to milestones); there is no need for raw GraphQL.

## Wayfinding operations

- Wayfinder maps use `wayfinder:map`; child tickets use exactly one of `wayfinder:research`, `wayfinder:prototype`, `wayfinder:grilling`, or `wayfinder:task`.
- Create all map tickets first, then attach each child under the map issue as its parent.
- Express blocking with Linear issue relations.
- The frontier is the map's open, unassigned children whose blocking relations are all closed. Claim one before work by assigning the ticket.
- Verify the map and its children by reading them, and inspect dependency edges through the issue's relations.

## Free-plan issue limit

The workspace is on Linear's free plan, which counts non-archived issues. When `save_issue` fails with "exceeded the free issue limit", archive old Done issues. The Linear MCP server has no archive tool, so use the authenticated `linctl` CLI:

```bash
linctl graphql -q 'query { issues(first: 15, filter: { state: { type: { eq: "completed" } } }, sort: [{ completedAt: { order: Ascending } }]) { nodes { identifier title } } }'
linctl graphql -q 'mutation { issueArchive(id: "ALE-123") { success } }'
```

Skip parent issues whose children are still open. `linctl graphql` also covers anything else the MCP tools lack.

## Relation direction gotcha

Agents keep entering blocking relations backwards. A relation points **from the blocker toward the blocked issue**: a blocking relation **from ALE-A to ALE-B** means **ALE-A must finish before ALE-B** (ALE-A is the prerequisite, ALE-B is the dependent). Equivalently, read it as "ALE-A blocks ALE-B."

When sequencing an expand→code→contract split (e.g. ALE-179), the correct edges are: expand blocks code, and code blocks contract. The expand migration is the frontier, not the contract. Before treating a Linear-reported "unblocked" issue as the frontier, cross-check it against the spec's stated ordering — if Linear's graph disagrees with the spec, the relations are inverted and must be fixed (remove the wrong edge, then add the correct one) before claiming the ticket.mise entire@0.13.1   [1/3] install

The `ryrt` version added `unhover()` calls, plus a line that hovered "Invite members" at 390px on purpose to "reproduce" the problem. In the diff images, the mismatch is the heading drawn in its fallback font. `app.css` loads Calistoga from Google Fonts over the network, so it can arrive after the first snapshot. The unhovers only helped because they added delay.

What I ran:
- The file on its own fails at 360×640 whether or not the unhovers are there, so this is already broken on `main`.
- The full suite without the unhovers failed twice.

- **Fresh token and socket/channel lifetime owned by the machine:** met. `fetchingToken` invokes the fetch, `connected` builds and joins the socket, `stopped` cleans up. Covered by the first-connect and reconnect-with-fresh-token tests.

- **Token-fetch timeout kept:** met (10,000 ms, new test).
- **401 is terminal:** met. Two tests: one through the real API client with a 401 response, and one where an existing connection stops for good.
- **Stale or late token discarded:** met. The invoked fetch is cancelled when its state exits; tests cover a timeout, a destroy during a fetch and a destroy during a reconnect.
- **Retired socket that revives is disconnected again:** met. Tests cover a replaced socket and a socket from a destroyed connection.
- **No competing reconnect loop:** met. Phoenix's own reconnect delay is still neutralised, and the new join-error/timeout test shows the machine stays out of channel rejoins.
- **Joins, rejoins and creation signals invalidate:** met (existing tests plus the new repeated-events test).
- **Destroy is idempotent:** met (new test).
- **No module-level actor:** met. Only the machine definition is at module level; `createActor` runs on each call (new two-connections test).
- **`NotificationCenter.svelte` unchanged:** met. `ryrt` doesn't touch it.
- **`connectNotificationRealtime(config) → { destroy }` preserved:** met. The exported types and signature are the same.

> `section-layout.browser.test.ts` screenshot baselines use the Calistoga display font, which `app.css` loads from Google Fonts. The test's `beforeAll` waits for that font to load. Screenshots taken before it loads, or offline, show the fallback font and fail. A pointer or hover state is not the cause.

- `constructSocket` is an `assign` that also builds the socket and calls `self.send`. It works and is tested, but side effects inside `assign` aren't idiomatic XState. Running the socket as an invoked `fromCallback` actor would let the state exit do the cleanup. That's a design change, so I didn't make it.

- The intermittent `intake-email-template-editor` timeout mentioned above.

  - `lookingUp`: fetching the saved payment method.
  - `lookupFailed`: that fetch itself failed.
  - `noSavedMethod`: the billing-portal fallback.
  - `ready`: the operator is choosing, or the charge is being submitted.

The fire-and-forget cache refresh behavior seems like a minor concern worth noting, possibly causing stale UI data briefly, but it's acceptable given the ticket's intent. For ALE-447, the embedded checkout work is the largest piece, so I'm thinking about whether to split it across two machines for the subagent.

Rather than merging intake and regular workshop checkout into one generic framework, I should keep them separate as the ticket suggests — two sequential subagents, one for intake checkout and one for the regular workshop register page, but I want to read the ticket first to confirm the actual scope.

## Problem Statement

A person paying for a Beginners' Workshop place, or a member registering for a regular Workshop, goes through an embedded Stripe Checkout widget whose lifecycle — initialize, mount, complete, confirm with Phoenix, retry, dispose — is spread across component flags and callbacks in two separate implementations: the Intake checkout widget with the Intake page's payment orchestration, and the regular-Workshop registration page. The critical safety rule — a failure confirming an already-completed payment must retry only confirmation and must never remount payment collection or start another payment attempt — exists only as carefully ordered procedural code. The regular-Workshop variant has no direct lifecycle test coverage at all.

## Solution

Each domain gets a component-scoped XState machine owning its embedded-widget lifecycle: initialization, mounted widget, confirmation, distinct failure targets with distinct retry targets, and disposal. The Intake orchestration (automatic one-shot payment start, session resume, pending-payment refresh, the Carried Fee confirm alternative) and the regular-Workshop registration flow keep their existing behavior and domain protocols, with retry-after-completion structurally impossible to misroute.

## User Stories

 1. As a person opening an Intake email link, I want payment to open automatically, so that I can pay without hunting for a button.
 2. As a person, I want the page's plain read to never reserve a place, so that previewing the email link does not take a Seat Hold.
 3. As a person with a live hold, I want the same Checkout session resumed, so that I am never charged twice for one place.
 4. As a person paying, I want the embedded widget to appear promptly with a loading indication, so that I know payment is starting.
 5. As a person whose widget fails to initialize, I want a retry that starts initialization over, so that a transient Stripe failure does not dead-end my place.
 6. As a person who completed payment in the widget, I want Phoenix to decide the outcome, so that the browser never claims a success Stripe did not confirm.
 7. As a person whose confirmation request fails after paying, I want to retry only the confirmation, so that I am never asked to pay a second time.
 8. As a person, I want the payment-in-progress refresh to reload Phoenix's view, so that a payment completed elsewhere is reflected on my page.
 9. As a person holding a workshop credit (Carried Fee), I want "Confirm my place" instead of Pay, so that my prepaid place is used rather than recharged.
10. As a person, I want fixed safe error copy when Stripe fails, so that error details that may contain credentials are never shown to me.
11. As a person navigating away mid-payment, I want the widget destroyed and late SDK results discarded, so that nothing leaks or fires into a dead page.
12. As a member registering for a regular Workshop, I want the same embedded lifecycle — initialization, mounted, failure, completion — so that registration is as reliable as Intake payment.
13. As a member whose regular-Workshop checkout fails to initialize, I want a retry that restarts initialization, so that I can recover without reloading the page.
14. As a developer, I want the retry distinction (initialization versus confirmation) encoded as distinct machine states, so that remounting payment collection after completion is unrepresentable.
15. As a developer, I want Stripe SDK resources behind the injected adapter, so that the machines are testable without Stripe.

 3. As a person with a live hold, I want the same Checkout session resumed, so that I am never charged twice for one place.

## What changed (all under `apps/web/src`)
- **New `lib/stripe/embedded-checkout-widget.ts`**: a domain-neutral XState actor wrapping Stripe's embedded widget. The widget lives exactly as long as the actor. When the actor stops, the widget is destroyed, a widget that resolves after the stop is destroyed instead of mounted, and late Stripe callbacks are dropped. A failure event carries no error, so raw SDK errors never leave the adapter.
- **New `lib/components/beginners-workshops/intake-checkout-machine.ts`** (the widget):
  - States: `dormant` → `collecting{loading, active}` → `initFailed` (retry goes back to `collecting`), and `confirming` → `confirmed`, or `confirmFailed` (retry goes back to `confirming` only).
  - Nothing leads from confirmation back to `collecting`.
  - `intakeCheckoutView()` returns a closed view with the same fixed copy as before.
- **`intake-checkout.svelte`** now only provides the factory, the container and the confirmation, then renders the view. **`intake-checkout-sdk.ts`** now just uses the shared factory type.
- **New `lib/beginners-workshops/intake-payment-machine.ts`** (the page):
  - `dormant` until `MOUNTED`, because `useMachine` starts actors during the server render. So the server render never POSTs and never arms the refresh timer.
  - Then two side-by-side regions. **`start`**: `waiting` → `starting` → `open`, `refused`, `spent` or `redirecting`. **`view`**: `routing` → `pay`, `confirmPlace`, `awaitingPayment` (refresh after `refreshMs`, re-armed on every new view) or `settled`.
  - `intakePaymentView()` returns a closed footer union plus the refusal.

I'll have the subagent complete that port and then verify and strengthen the tests, since the ticket calls for a full lifecycle component.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e3aaec634ffe3772yVCl73DTlD" state="completed">
The regular-Workshop half of ALE-447 is ported and committed as **`xly`** on `feature/ale-449-notification-recovery`. Check, lint, build and the full unit suite are green. No E2E test was run, because none covers `/workshops/[id]/register`.

## Files changed (all in commit `xly`)
- **New:**
  - `apps/web/src/lib/components/workshops/workshop-registration-checkout-machine.ts` and its `.test.ts`
  - `workshop-registration-checkout-sdk.ts` and its `.test.ts`
  - `workshop-registration-checkout.svelte` and its `.browser.test.ts`
- **Edited:**
  - `routes/(public)/workshops/[id]/register/+page.svelte`: the `onMount`, the `flowError`/`checkoutInitializing` flags and the inline Stripe code are gone. The page now renders `{#key data.checkoutSessionId}<WorkshopRegistrationCheckout clientSecret=REDACTED />{/key}`.
  - `docs/agents/where-to-look.md`: a new regular-Workshop registration row, placed after the express-checkout row.
  - `docs/agents/tech-stack.md`: the XState line now lists this machine.

The shared `embedded-checkout-widget.ts` and the Intake files are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
| Criterion | Met | How verified |
|---|---|---|
| Same lifecycle (init, mounted, failure, completion) | Yes | Phases are `dormant` → `collecting.loading` → `collecting.active`, plus `initFailed`. Completion stays with Stripe, which redirects to the session's return URL. Machine and browser tests cover this. |
| Init retry restarts init without a reload | Yes | `initFailed` → `RETRY` → `collecting` creates a new widget for the same session. Tested at both levels: two `create` calls with the same secret, and one mount. |
| Flow-error surface and visible behavior preserved | Yes, with one copy change (see below) | Same "Registration error" alert, "Loading payment form..." loader and `#workshop-checkout` container with the same classes. Browser tests check them. |
| Late widget or session after disposal is destroyed; late callbacks dropped | Yes | Machine tests: stop mid-init, then resolve → `destroy` is called and `mount` is not; a late reject after stop is ignored; no snapshot is emitted after stop. The browser test unmounts mid-init. |
| Client secret and raw SDK errors never logged or shown | Yes | The adapter's `WIDGET.FAILED` carries no error, and the copy is fixed. Tests reject with an error containing `cs_test_secret` and assert it never reaches the context or the DOM. |
| Procedural flags removed | Yes | The page no longer has its own Stripe code or state. |
| No Stripe before `MOUNTED` | Yes | Machine test: settle, then assert `create` was not called. |

## Behavior changes a reviewer should know about
1. **Error copy is now fixed.** Main showed the raw `error.message` from Stripe, or "Failed to initialize secure payment. Please refresh and try again." when `loadStripe` returned null. Every init failure now shows "Failed to initialize checkout. Please try again." This was main's own fallback copy. The two unavailable messages are unchanged.
2. **New "Try again" button** on init failure. It is not offered when payment is unavailable or the session is missing.
3. **Unavailable states render during SSR.** With no Stripe key or no session, the error appears in the server render. Main first rendered the loader and replaced it with the error on mount.
4. **The component is keyed by `checkoutSessionId`.** A re-load that yields a new session, such as client navigation to another workshop, now mounts a fresh widget. Main's one-shot `onMount` kept the old one.
5. **The widget mounts into a bound element** rather than the `"#workshop-checkout"` selector. The id stays so the page's global iframe CSS still applies.

## How the port differs from rsor's version
- It uses the umbrella's adapter, so `WIDGET.FAILED` has no error and there is no `failureMessage(event.error)`.
- `dormant` replaces `mounting`. The context holds no error string, and there are two unavailable phases (`paymentUnavailable`, `sessionMissing`), each with fixed copy in a closed `PRESENTATION` table. These states are deliberately not `final`: the host always sends `MOUNTED`, and an earlier version that marked them final logged "sent to stopped actor" warnings.
- The view is a `workshopRegistrationCheckoutView()` that mirrors `intakeCheckoutView`, instead of rsor's `…Phase()` plus a context error.
- The SDK now exports `redirectingEmbeddedCheckout(load)`, which passes `{ clientSecret }` only. Leaving out `onComplete` matters because Stripe rejects it for sessions that always redirect. Injecting the loader lets that be unit-tested: the `anti-slop/no-module-mocking` lint rule rejected a `vi.mock` version.
- The tests reuse the umbrella's `fakeStripe()`/`deferred()`/`stripeStub()` patterns. They add a "completion and repeated events change nothing" case, a mount-throws case, a late-reject case, and a loading-visible browser test.

## Verification (run from `apps/web`)
- `mise exec -- pnpm check`: 0 errors, 19 warnings, none in touched files.
- `mise exec -- pnpm lint`: exit 0, no findings in touched files.
- `oxfmt` on the touched files: done.
- `mise exec -- pnpm test:unit --run src/lib/components/workshops/workshop-registration-checkout`: 3 files, 16 tests passed.
- `mise exec -- pnpm build`: passed.
- Full `mise exec -- pnpm test:unit --run`: 117 files, 1199 tests passed, exit 0. Vitest printed "close timed out", and some `derived_inert` warnings came from other suites.
- **E2E: not run.** A grep of `apps/web/e2e` found no spec that visits the public register or confirmation page. I didn't touch the shared widget, so I didn't re-run the Beginners' Workshop journey or money specs.
- **Svelte autofixer:** no issues for the component. For the page, I submitted a condensed version: the full new script and the changed markup, without the unchanged layout. It reported no issues. Its only suggestion was to replace `bind:this` with an attachment, which I kept so it matches `intake-checkout.svelte`.

## Suggested AGENTS.md note
> Public regular-Workshop registration's embedded Checkout (ALE-447) is `workshopRegistrationCheckoutMachine`, rendered by `workshop-registration-checkout.svelte` and keyed by Checkout Session id. Its sessions always redirect on completion, so its SDK factory (`redirectingEmbeddedCheckout`) must never forward the widget actor's `onComplete`, and the machine has no confirmation phase. It shares only `lib/stripe/embedded-checkout-widget.ts` with the Intake machines. No E2E test covers `/workshops/[id]/register`, so its component and machine tests are the only regression net.

## Noticed but left alone
- Nothing end-to-end tests the public register or confirmation flow.
- The `derived_inert` warnings and Vitest's hanging-close message in the full suite were already there; I didn't investigate them.
- The workspace has uncommitted `.agents/skills/gitbutler/*` edits that aren't mine, and I didn't touch them.
</subagent>

 ## Navigation
 
 - Workshop non-response is normal waiting, not an alert: `workshop-people.svelte` renders one People roster with visible counted status filters from `rosterGroups` and neutral payment/confirmation guidance; reserve “Needs attention” for workshop issues and failed refunds. Keep each person in one rendered list rather than adding a second response list or disclosure; payment deadlines and automatic outcomes stay Phoenix-owned.
 
-- Beginners' Workshop section pages scroll as a document below `lg`; only desktop constrains the dashboard and panels to the viewport. Keep the responsive height/overflow chain aligned in the dashboard layout, `section-shell.svelte`, and list panels: fixed phone heights let filters squeeze the list to zero. `section-layout.browser.test.ts` covers initial and scrolled views with tracked Chromium/macOS screenshot baselines; review updates, then rerun without `-u`.

Keep the responsive height/overflow chain aligned in the dashboard layout, `section-shell.svelte`, and list panels: fixed phone heights let filters squeeze the list to zero. `section-layout.browser.test.ts` covers initial and scrolled views with tracked Chromium/macOS screenshot baselines; review updates, then rerun without `-u`. Its `beforeAll` waits for the Calistoga web font (loaded from Google Fonts); a mismatch showing the fallback heading font is a font-load problem, not hover state.
 
 - Beginners' Workshop dialogs share `lib/components/beginners-workshops/workshop-dialog.svelte`: below 640px they slide up as full-width bottom sheets; desktop stays centered. Keep the existing Dialog/AlertDialog roots so focus handling and destructive-confirmation semantics survive, and put responsive layout changes in this shared wrapper.
 
 - Form controls use `bg-field` (`--field-background` in `apps/web/src/app.css`) for an opaque white light-mode surface and a themed dark-mode surface, including date and phone picker triggers; keep this separate from the page background and the `--input` border token.

content.text: I unapplied the ale-449 branch from the main workspace since it's now in a worktree, leaving the gitbutler skill edits in the main checkout untouched. I'm noting that the ale-447 lane has duplicates and a model config issue, and none of this has been pushed yet.

All five ALE-446 tickets are implemented on `feature/ale-449-notification-recovery`, in the GitButler worktree at `~/.gitbutler-worktrees/dhc-dashboard/feature-ale-449-notification-recovery`. Check, lint, build and the full unit + browser suite (1199 tests) pass on the final commit. Nothing is pushed and no PR is open.

**Commits** (oldest first, on top of the original `ryrt`):
- **ALE-449** (`pzln`): notification recovery. `ryrt` already met the ticket, so this commit only adds the missing edge-case tests. It also replaces `ryrt`'s hover workaround in the `section-layout` snapshot test: the real cause was a web font (Calistoga) that hadn't loaded yet.
- **ALE-448** (`kwqu`): `save-machine.ts` for Training Announcement saves. A schedule refusal never triggers the copy write, a copy failure after a saved schedule is its own stage, and retry resumes the stage that failed.
- **ALE-450** (`txkt`): `reactivation-machine.ts`, with TanStack Query still owning reads and cache. The modal is now presentational only.
- **ALE-451** (`tnrw`): `item-workbench-machine.ts`. The remote-form command path and draft rebasing are kept, and a late command answer can no longer land on another Item.
- **ALE-447** (`uqxk` + `xlyr`): Intake page and widget machines, plus the public Workshop registration machine. They share only a small Stripe widget adapter. Once a payment completes, a failed confirmation retries only the confirmation.
- `rqzs`: AGENTS.md notes for these machines, including that `useMachine` starts actors during SSR, so each machine waits for `MOUNTED` before doing anything.

**Verification:** each subagent ran check, lint, oxfmt, focused tests and build. These E2E specs pass: training-announcements, member-reactivation, inventory-item-management, inventory-operator-loan-queue, and beginners-workshop journey and money. No E2E spec covers `/workshops/[id]/register`, so that page relies on its new machine and component tests.

**Behaviour changes to review:**
- **Reactivation:**
  - A failed saved-method lookup now shows an error instead of the billing-portal fallback.
  - The lookup no longer retries 3 times.
  - The dialog can't be dismissed while a charge is submitting.
  - The members-table dialog loses its close animation.
- **Items page:**
  - A late command answer only updates the cache.
  - Leaving the create page during the success flash no longer navigates to the new Item.
  - List refreshes are no longer awaited.
- **Intake page:**
  - If Phoenix's view asks for payment again later, the person gets a manual Pay button instead of a silent remount.
  - "Try again" is now a button that tells the machine to retry, rather than a form submit.
- **Workshop registration:**
  - Stripe init errors show fixed copy instead of the raw message.
  - There's a new "Try again" button.
  - The component is keyed by Checkout Session id, so a new session gets a fresh widget.

**Needs your decision:** while this was running, another session created `feature/ale-447-convert-embedded-checkout-lifecycles-to` (commit `rsor`, with its own worktree). It implements ALE-447 independently and also edits AGENTS.md. Our Intake half started from its design, and the registration half was ported from it. I didn't touch it. You probably want to drop it, or the two will conflict when merged.

**Other changes:**
- In the main checkout, I unapplied `feature/ale-449-notification-recovery` from the workspace so it could live in the worktree. Your uncommitted `.agents/skills/gitbutler/*` edits there are untouched.
- In Linear, ALE-446 through ALE-451 are now "In Review".
- Your `opencode.json` points `build` (and `docs`, `indexer`, `small_model`) at `toast/global.openai.gpt-6-luna`, which doesn't exist; the provider has `toast/openai.gpt-6-luna`. Every subagent here therefore ran on Opus 5.5 medium, as you chose. I left the config alone.

**Noticed, not fixed:**
- Svelte `derived_inert` warnings appear in a few suites (the Training Announcements rail tests and one Beginners' Workshop journey E2E test); they were there before this branch.
- `intake-email-template-editor.browser.test.ts` times out now and then.
- Vitest prints a "close timed out" message after every run.
- The notification machine starts its socket from inside an `assign`. That works and is tested but isn't idiomatic XState.
- The section-layout snapshots need network access to Google Fonts.
